verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_seed_products_and_orders: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names mostly explain themselves (updateAfterSalePreview, refundedBySku, remainingPayable, uiExecuteImport) and section banners help. But it is one 3.5k-line file of long template-string HTML with inline handlers, and the allocation/tail-difference logic has almost no comments.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One new 3502-line file, which caps this at accept. The UI copies business logic: updateAfterSalePreview re-implements refund allocation and the all-refunded check, and refundedBySku is built twice in the modal code. Handlers are attached as window.* globals.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Inputs are validated (Number.isInteger qty, phone regex) and import failures are reported. Money is float math with round2 (round2(order.payable - order.refundedAmount)). Hidden tests failed test_seed_products_and_orders and test_cart_rejects_out_of_stock_and_over_stock.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: Shows subtotal/payable/refunded, a rules banner, status badges, a refund preview and toasts with readable reasons. submitAfterSaleModal calls requestAfterSale and uiExecuteImport imports without any confirm step, so refund and import overwrite have no confirmation.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: The UI calls shopTestAPI.* for mutations and stats look derived from records. Money is float with round2 rather than integer cents, and the after-sale preview duplicates the allocation formula instead of reusing the core function.
